proof_method_executed: A 5-gate structural audit over the submitted tree (producers of key_entry_clear, producers of flush_keyvault, the kv module port list and its top-level connection, every boot-stage-like signal name anywhere in the RTL and RDL, and the in-tree specification assignment of the KeyVault clearing duty), plus a directed single-DUT simulation of src/keyvault/rtl/kv.sv that provisions an unlocked entry and measures its readability across every stage-like input the module exposes, with an asserted control confirming the debug/scan clearing path does work. Gates evaluated: 5 of 5. Simulation controls: 2 asserted, 0 failures. The audit gate that decides the case, gate 4, returned boot_stage_signal_hits_in_rtl=0.
result_summary:
The claim requires two independent things to be true: that a boot-stage transition indication exists which a per-entry clear could be driven from, and that an in-tree requirement assigns that clear to hardware. Neither holds.

The simulation confirms the retention the candidate describes, and does so at the module's own read response port so that what is measured is what a crypto engine would receive. An entry provisioned through a write client with dest_valid granted to the HMAC-key destination, and deliberately left unlocked, reads back 0xa5a51234 with rd_error=0. It still reads back 0xa5a51234 while fw_update_rst_window is asserted (probe_retained_in_fw_update_window=1) and still reads back 0xa5a51234 after a full core_only_rst_b pulse (probe_retained_across_core_only_reset=1). The control then shows the module's clearing path is not broken: a debugUnlock_or_scan_mode_switch pulse overwrites the entry with 0xaaaaaaaa, the debug value the module selects when CLEAR_SECRETS.sel_debug_value is at its reset value.

Retention alone is not a violation, and this plan pre-committed not to treat it as one. What settles the case is the audit. src/keyvault/rtl/kv.sv:159-161 derives key_entry_clear from exactly three terms: kv_multi_write_err, the software-poked KEY_CTRL.clear bit qualified by ~lock_wr_q & ~lock_use_q, and a self-hold across an in-flight control write. src/keyvault/rtl/kv.sv:122-123 derives flush_keyvault from exactly two terms: debugUnlock_or_scan_mode_switch, and cptra_in_debug_scan_mode gated by CLEAR_SECRETS.wr_debug_values. Neither expression contains any stage-dependent term (key_entry_clear_stage_dependent_terms=0, flush_keyvault_stage_dependent_terms=0).

That is not, by itself, a defect: the clear could only be driven from an input, and the kv module has none that could carry a stage indication. Its port list is 23 ports (kv_boot_stage_ports=0), all 23 connected at src/integration/rtl/caliptra_top.sv:1189-1215 (kv_instantiation_stage_ports=0). The stage-like inputs it does have are reset and window signals, which is precisely why the simulation exercised those and nothing else.

Nor does such a signal exist elsewhere and merely fail to reach the KeyVault, which would have been a routing gap worth reporting. A case-insensitive sweep of every .sv, .svh, .v and .rdl file under src/ for boot_stage, boot_flow, stable_owner, stable_owner_key_en, boot_flow_key_clear, boot_flow_error, rt_stage, fmc_stage, rom_stage, stage_transition and kv_monitor_alert returns boot_stage_signal_hits_in_rtl=0. The one OCP LOCK mode indication that does exist, CPTRA_HW_CONFIG.OCP_LOCK_MODE_en, is driven from the ss_ocp_lock_en integration strap at src/soc_ifc/rtl/soc_ifc_top.sv:521, making it a static capability bit for the whole power cycle rather than a transition event; it has no reference in src/keyvault/rtl/kv.sv (ocp_lock_mode_references_in_kv_sv=0). No boot-stage concept is represented in this hardware at all.

The in-tree specifications then assign the duty elsewhere. src/keyvault/config/keyvault.md:14 enumerates the clearing mechanisms exhaustively: entries in the KV must be cleared via control register, or by de-assertion of pwrgood. Both are implemented; the control-register path is the KEY_CTRL.clear term in gate 1, and pwrgood is the hard_reset_b resetsignal on the key fields at src/keyvault/rtl/kv_reg.rdl:22. The only hardware-initiated clearing the specifications require is on a debug or scan mode transition, at docs/CaliptraIntegrationSpecification.md:249-250, which src/keyvault/rtl/kv.sv:122-123 implements and the simulation control verifies. A search for a boot-stage clearing requirement across the KeyVault document and both specifications returns spec_boot_stage_clear_requirements=0. Stage-specific asset policy is assigned to ROM: src/keyvault/config/keyvault.md:209-210 marks KV22 and KV16 locked for writes until warm reset as a ROM requirement, and :225 states Caliptra ROM shall lock KV22 for writes once it has derived the HEK there.

Finally, the retention the simulation measured across the firmware-update reset is the specified behavior, not an oversight. docs/CaliptraHardwareSpecification.md:63 states that on a firmware-update reset only the RISC-V core is reset and all registers within the targets are intact after the reset. A KeyVault that wiped entries there would contradict that sentence.

impact: No security impact, because no security property of this design is violated. The mechanism the candidate says is missing is not a hardware feature this design is specified to have: the KeyVault clearing mechanisms are enumerated in src/keyvault/config/keyvault.md:14 as the control register and pwrgood de-assertion, both implemented, plus the debug/scan transition flush required by docs/CaliptraIntegrationSpecification.md:249-250 and implemented at src/keyvault/rtl/kv.sv:122-123.

The stage isolation the candidate describes is a firmware obligation in this architecture, not a hardware one. An earlier stage that must not leak an entry to the next stage has two in-tree mechanisms available to it: set KEY_CTRL.clear to wipe the entry, or set KEY_CTRL.lock_use, which src/keyvault/rtl/kv.sv:233-234 makes suppress the read for every client. Both are reachable from the microcontroller through the KEY_CTRL register. An earlier stage that leaves an entry unlocked and unwiped has declined to use them.

Observation recorded while auditing, not a finding of this case: the lock fields cannot be set by hardware even if a future policy wanted them to be. src/keyvault/rtl/kv_reg.rdl:28-31 declares lock_wr and lock_use as sw=rw; swwel=true; hw=r, with no hwset, hw=w or we property (lock_fields_hardware_settable=0). Any retention policy added later would have to extend the register interface, not merely wire a new signal to it.
security_impact_assessment.bypassed_feature: None. No boot-stage transition clear is specified for this hardware, and the clearing paths that are specified are present and were measured working.
attacker_model: Later-stage Caliptra firmware executing at supervisor mode on the microcontroller was assumed, reading an entry that an earlier stage provisioned and left unlocked. The measurement confirms such a read succeeds. It is not a bypass: the earlier stage held both KEY_CTRL.clear and KEY_CTRL.lock_use and used neither, so no hardware control was defeated and no isolation the design promises was crossed.

evidence.key_observation: Measured at the kv module's read response port for an unlocked entry 0 provisioned with dest_valid granted to the HMAC-key destination: after provisioning read_data=0xa5a51234 with rd_error=0; with fw_update_rst_window=1 read_data=0xa5a51234 (probe_retained_in_fw_update_window=1); after a core_only_rst_b pulse read_data=0xa5a51234 (probe_retained_across_core_only_reset=1); after a debugUnlock_or_scan_mode_switch pulse read_data=0xaaaaaaaa, matching the debug value the module selects. checks_run=2 checks_failed=0. Structural audit: key_entry_clear_producer_terms=3 with key_entry_clear_stage_dependent_terms=0, flush_keyvault_producer_terms=3 with flush_keyvault_stage_dependent_terms=0, kv_port_count=23 with kv_boot_stage_ports=0, kv_instantiation_connected_ports=23 with kv_instantiation_stage_ports=0, boot_stage_signal_hits_in_rtl=0, ocp_lock_mode_references_in_kv_sv=0, spec_boot_stage_clear_requirements=0, spec_hardware_clear_conditions=2, lock_fields_hardware_settable=0, audit_conclusion=no_boot_stage_transition_exists_and_none_is_required.
evidence.clearing_mechanisms_present: KEY_CTRL.clear per entry, qualified by ~lock_wr_q & ~lock_use_q at src/keyvault/rtl/kv.sv:160; kv_multi_write_err at src/keyvault/rtl/kv.sv:159; the debug/scan flush at src/keyvault/rtl/kv.sv:122-123 writing the debug value into every entry and dword; and pwrgood de-assertion, which is the hard_reset_b resetsignal on the key data fields at src/keyvault/rtl/kv_reg.rdl:22. Read suppression through KEY_CTRL.lock_use at src/keyvault/rtl/kv.sv:233-234 provides isolation without a wipe.

non_findings: Missing per-entry boot-stage transition clear as an exploitable finding: withdrawn. Gate 3 shows the kv module exposes no port that could carry a stage indication (kv_boot_stage_ports=0 over 23 ports, all 23 connected at the top level), and gate 4 shows no boot-stage signal name exists anywhere in the tree's RTL or RDL (boot_stage_signal_hits_in_rtl=0). There is no stage transition in this hardware to clear on.

A stage signal existing in the tree but failing to reach the KeyVault: withdrawn, as the plan pre-committed. This was the more interesting possibility, since a routing gap would have been reportable. The sweep over boot_stage, boot_flow, stable_owner, stable_owner_key_en, boot_flow_key_clear, boot_flow_error, rt_stage, fmc_stage, rom_stage, stage_transition and kv_monitor_alert returns zero hits, case-insensitively, across every .sv, .svh, .v and .rdl under src/.

CPTRA_HW_CONFIG.OCP_LOCK_MODE_en as a stage indication: withdrawn. It is driven from the ss_ocp_lock_en integration strap at src/soc_ifc/rtl/soc_ifc_top.sv:521, so it is constant for the power cycle and marks a configuration, not a transition. It is also absent from src/keyvault/rtl/kv.sv entirely. It is deliberately excluded from the gate 4 stage sweep and reported separately so the negative result is precise rather than overbroad.

KeyVault data surviving fw_update_rst_window as a violation: withdrawn, exactly as the plan pre-committed before the measurement was taken. The retention is measured (probe_retained_in_fw_update_window=1) and it is the specified behavior: docs/CaliptraHardwareSpecification.md:63 states all registers within the targets are intact after a firmware-update reset. The window's actual role in this module is visible at src/keyvault/rtl/kv.sv:176-177, where it qualifies lock_wr_q and lock_use_q to avoid a reset-domain-crossing violation on the lock bits.

KeyVault data surviving a core_only_rst_b pulse as a violation: withdrawn on the same specification sentence. core_only_rst_b resets the microcontroller and the KEY_CTRL lock fields, which is why src/keyvault/rtl/kv_reg.rdl:28-31 names it as their resetsignal, while the key data fields reset on hard_reset_b per src/keyvault/rtl/kv_reg.rdl:22. Clearing key data there would contradict the specification, not satisfy it.

Absence of a hardware retention-exception set for OCP Lock slots: withdrawn as a consequence of the above. With no stage transition to key it from, a retention mask has nothing to select between. The OCP Lock slot policy the KeyVault document does state is assigned to ROM at src/keyvault/config/keyvault.md:209-210 and :225, and its mechanism is the software-writable lock_wr bit.

The inability of hardware to set lock_wr or lock_use, from src/keyvault/rtl/kv_reg.rdl:28-31 declaring them hw=r with no hwset, hw=w or we: recorded as an observation about how any future retention policy would have to be built, not asserted as a defect. Nothing in the tree tries to set them from hardware, so no current logic is broken by it.

kv_multi_write_err clearing every entry at once, visible at src/keyvault/rtl/kv.sv:159 where the term is not qualified per entry: noticed while enumerating gate 1 and out of scope here. It concerns the blast radius of a write-collision response, not boot-stage isolation, and is not assessed by this case.
conclusion: False alarm. The retention the candidate describes is real and was measured directly: an unlocked entry provisioned by one stage remains readable by its granted destination across the firmware-update reset window and across a microcontroller-only reset. That retention violates no property this design is required to enforce. There is no boot-stage transition indication anywhere in the submitted tree, in RTL or RDL, so nothing exists for a per-entry transition clear to be driven from; the kv module exposes no port that could carry one; and the in-tree specifications enumerate the KeyVault clearing mechanisms as the control register and pwrgood de-assertion, with hardware-initiated clearing required only on a debug or scan mode transition, which the module implements and which the simulation control confirms working. Stage-specific asset policy is assigned to ROM firmware, whose mechanism is the software-writable lock_wr and lock_use bits and the per-entry clear bit. An earlier stage that leaves an entry unlocked has declined the isolation the design offers it rather than been denied it by hardware. What is worth recording for a future reviewer is that the lock fields are declared hw=r, so a hardware-enforced retention policy could not be added by wiring a signal alone; it would need a register interface change as well.
